comment: R1: full review of the example (docs/acceptance-tests.md, M2 test environment). anchor 'label:<field label>' is replaced by the mock with the [kp:<id>] / [opt:<id>] tag it finds in the design text.

findings.title: Average check does not measure the stated goal
findings.evidence: The key metric of the A/B test is the average check, while the goal is to cut waste and lost sales.
findings.why: A forecast can raise the average check while waste grows, so the test can approve a model that misses the goal.
findings.fix: Make the primary metric waste plus lost sales in money per store-day.

findings.title: Split by distribution center leaves too few units to detect +0.3%
findings.evidence: The chosen split assigns whole distribution centers to groups, but the design has only a handful of them.
findings.why: With few units the minimum detectable effect is far above +0.3%, so the test cannot confirm the expected gain.
findings.fix: Estimate the minimum detectable effect for the number of distribution centers, or split by matched store subsets.

findings.title: Control metrics have no thresholds
findings.evidence: Control metrics are listed without the values that would stop the test.
findings.why: Without thresholds a harmful rollout is noticed late.
findings.fix: Set a stop threshold for each control metric.

findings.title: Out-of-stock is called costlier than overstock, but neither cost is estimated
findings.evidence: The design says out-of-stock hurts more than overstock without numbers.
findings.why: The loss and the decision threshold depend on the ratio of the two costs.
findings.fix: Estimate the cost of one unit of out-of-stock and of overstock per category.

findings.title: Antigoals are not stated
findings.evidence: The problem statement lists goals but nothing the system must not do.
findings.why: Without antigoals the scope grows and trade-offs are argued case by case.
findings.fix: List two or three antigoals, for example no price optimization in this project.
